description: Three separate requests for design sign-off on 'the settings redesign' land in one week, from three people, in three threads, with only the middle one addressed to the user — and the other two are visible restatements of it. The summary is nearly impossible to get wrong; the citation is easy to get wrong.

events.text: Engineering can't start the settings redesign build until design sign-off lands. Who owns that sign-off? Asking so I can chase the right person.
Noor owns it. I'd ask directly rather than in here, this channel is noisy.

events.context_label: Settings redesign — design sign-off needed to start build
events.text: Noor — I need your sign-off on the settings redesign specs before engineering can start the build. Specifically the two-column form layout and the new save-behavior spec. Sprint planning is Thursday the 18th; if I don't have sign-off by then the work slides a sprint. This is the only thing I need from you.
FYI the settings redesign is still waiting on design sign-off, which is apparently blocking the build. Flagging in case it's fallen off someone's list.
Sprint planning is at 14:00 today. Still no design sign-off on settings, so I'm provisionally planning without it.
Unrelated to the sign-off: I've updated the icon set in the shared library, so pull the latest before you export anything. No action needed beyond that.

ground_truth.notes: Four artifacts describe the same obligation and only one of them is the ask. The correct citation is gmail:gm-thread-dw1-a:msg-1 — the message that is addressed to the user, names the specific artifacts to sign off, and states the deadline and consequence. Each distractor fails for a different reason: ev-dw1-001 asks who the owner is rather than asking the user (and predates knowing it is them); ev-dw1-002 is a third party naming the owner, not making the request; ev-dw1-004 is a bystander's FYI in a different channel; ev-dw1-005 is a status update stating the consequence, not the ask. Note that ev-dw1-002 even instructs Callum to move the request out of Slack, which is the in-fixture explanation for why the real ask is the email. A pending item with a correct description and any of these four citations is a citation failure against AC-6 and must not be scored as a pass.
